sections.h2: Where is Troup County and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Troup County sits on Georgia's western edge against the Alabama line. LaGrange is the seat and the biggest city. Of 446 square miles, 414 are land, and the Piedmont terrain runs through all of it. Interstate 85 and Interstate 185 cross the county, with U.S. 27 and several state routes, so Atlanta commuters and Columbus-area workers both choose to live here. Heard, Coweta, Meriwether and Harris counties adjoin it, and so do Chambers and Randolph counties in Alabama.

The General Assembly drew the county lines on June 9, 1826, after the Creek ceded the land in the 1825 Treaty of Indian Springs, per Wikipedia's county entry. Cotton mills built around LaGrange in the late 1800s anchored local work for generations. Textile jobs eventually moved overseas, and auto parts suppliers serving the nearby Kia plant took up some of the slack. West Point Lake and Callaway Gardens bring in visitors.

Three cities sit inside the county: LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point. Long Cane, Mountville, Harrisonville and Abbottsford are unincorporated communities. A bungalow in LaGrange, a lake-area lot near West Point and a farm parcel outside Hogansville each draw a different buyer, which matters when you plan a sale with a tax bill still open. Public schools run through the Troup County School District, and a five-member commission, with a chairman chosen countywide, governs.

sections.h2: How many people and homes does Troup County have?
sections.html:
Census estimates for mid-2025 put Troup County at 72,844 people, which is 4.9% above the April 2020 base. Roughly 61 of every 100 housing units are lived in by their owners, and QuickFacts lists the middle owner-occupied value at $217,200.

Population was 50,003 in 1980, 58,779 in 2000 and 67,044 in 2010, so growth has been steady for decades. The 2020 census counted 28,721 housing units with 8.4% vacant, and about four in ten occupied units were rented. People 65 and older make up 17.8% of residents, which keeps estate sales and inherited houses in the mix.

sections.h2: Which Troup County office does what?
sections.html:
Your tax passes through two separate desks. One collects money. The other, a citizens board served by the Property Appraisal Department, decides what the parcel is worth.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 883-1620, open on weekdays from 8 to 5, for bills, mobile home and timber tax, and tag renewals.
  • Property Appraisal: (706) 883-1625, at 100 Ridley Avenue, Suite 2100, LaGrange, for values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens.

The county's appraisal FAQ describes the assessors as a part-time citizens board, so a call may land on voicemail and be returned later. That board picks the Chief Appraiser, answers to state law and the Georgia Constitution, and gets its budget from the county commission. You can pay on the county's online payment page, which lists a Property Taxes option, or by phone with the tax office.

sections.h2: When are Troup County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Troup's property tax page names November 15 as the official deadline, with penalties and interest piling up after it. State revenue officials let counties move the statewide default, so read the date printed on the bill you actually receive.

Georgia freezes market value as of January 1 and then taxes 40% of it. Millage comes from the school board, the county governing authority and any other body that covers your parcel. A sample calculation on the appraisal FAQ uses .030260 as the rate and takes off exemptions first. Mobile homes and timber reach the same collector on their own timetables.

  • The state ratio is 40%, applied to market value.
  • One mill means a dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value.
  • A higher value or a dropped exemption can lift a bill while the rate stays flat.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Troup County value?
sections.html:
Appeals grow out of the yearly assessment notice, and you get 45 days after the notice date shown on its face. Once that passes, you lose the chance to challenge that year's number.

The appraisers say they want sales records, photos of similar houses that changed hands lately, and whatever else supports your figure. A Board of Equalization hearing usually follows. Grand jurors name its members, who are neighbors and fellow owners, and filing is free. Arbitration is the other lane: each party hires one arbitrator and splits a third. Going on to Superior Court adds a $25.00 filing fee, per the county FAQ.

After a board or court rules, the assessors cannot move that value for two years without walking the parcel themselves.

sections.h2: Which Troup County exemptions are worth a look?
sections.html:
Homestead filings are taken from the first of January through April 1. Miss the window and you forfeit the benefit for that year. Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 hands out the forms and quotes the amounts.

Other special exemptions are kept in the same office. The state's county facts page adds two quirks: skipping a return means you are deemed to have returned the same property at last year's final value, and freeport relief for inventory needs a local vote. A move means filing again for the new address.

  • Be the owner and the occupant on the first day of the year.
  • A refund claim for a tax wrongly assessed has a three-year limit from payment.
  • Mobile homes sit on a separate location permit and return cycle.

sections.h2: How should a Troup County seller handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the collector before a closing date is set, and let the attorney or title agent settle it out of your proceeds. The year's bill is addressed to the person who held title on New Year's Day, so an autumn sale can send you a statement for a house you no longer own unless the settlement sheet splits it.

The tax commissioner's news page posts a courtesy tax sale list and a note that excess funds after such a sale go only to the record owner at that time or to other lienholders. A house that sat for several years as a rental, an inheritance or a vacancy can carry more than one year of bills, so ask for each year in writing.

A cash buyer can close with a balance still open because the payoff comes off the price. Lay the closing statement beside the payoff letter and check them line by line.

faqs.q: How do I phone the Troup County tax office?
faqs.a: Dial (706) 883-1620. Questions about value or exemptions go to Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625.

faqs.q: Is November 15 the Troup County payment deadline?
faqs.a: Yes. The county tax page calls November 15 the official deadline and says penalties and interest follow it. Confirm against your own statement.

faqs.q: How long can I challenge a Troup County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. A late filing forfeits the right for that year, and appeals cannot be filed without a notice.

faqs.q: When does Troup County take homestead applications?
faqs.a: From New Year's Day through April 1. Anything filed later waits for the next year.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax if I sell in October?
faqs.a: The person who owned it on January 1 is billed. Settle it at closing and ask the tax commissioner for the payoff letter first.
